bib.title: Doc-to-LoRA: Learning to Instantly Internalize Contexts

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Doc-to-LoRA: Learning to Instantly Internalize Contexts" (D2L). Rujikorn Charakorn, Edoardo Cetin, Shinnosuke Uesaka (intern; Minerva University), Robert T. Lange. Sakana AI, Tokyo (Uesaka also Minerva Univ., California). arXiv:2602.15902v1 [cs.CL], 13 Feb 2026; header says "Preprint. February 19, 2026." The acknowledgements mention "anonymous reviewers", but no venue is printed. Code: github.com/SakanaAI/doc-to-lora.

COVERAGE: 28 of 28 pages extracted, 97,392 chars. I read the body, Appendices A-H and the Appendix D/E text, and the table values and captions. I skimmed the references and the code listings (pseudocode and module print-out, about the last 15K chars) and did not read them closely. Figures are only partly readable as text (axis labels), so I did not run figures.py. The Fig 3/4 curves are not quoted for that reason.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- D2L is a hypernetwork that turns a document into a LoRA adapter in one forward pass, so later queries run without the document in context. It is meta-trained to imitate context distillation (CD).
  number: none
  setup: base gemma-2-2b-it; 309M trainable hypernetwork parameters; rank-8 LoRA per 8K-token chunk, applied to the MLP down-projection.
  quote: "D2L generates a LoRA adapter for a target LLM, enabling subsequent queries to be answered without re-consuming the original context, reducing latency and KV-cache memory consumption"
  where: Abstract, p1; Sec 5 setup, p5.
- Sub-second internalization beats CD on latency. On SQuAD, D2L takes under 1 s. Oracle CD (optimized on the target query) takes about 40 s. Vanilla CD with generated queries takes over 100 s.
  number: under 1 s; about 40 s; over 100 s
  setup: gemma-2-2b-it, SQuAD, single H200, up to 500 test samples.
  quote: "D2L instantly internalizes context information within less than a second using either batched or iterative mode. CD (oracle) uses around 40 seconds to internalize information ... totaling more than 100 seconds."
  where: Sec 5.1.1, p5.
- Quality on SQuAD reaches 82.5% of the in-context upper bound. That is roughly what LLMLingua-2 gets at 40% context length, but D2L removes the context entirely.
  number: 82.5%; 40%
  setup: gemma-2-2b-it, word-level ROUGE-L F1 relative to the base model with context.
  quote: "achieving 82.5% relative performance compared to the ICL upper bound on the SQuAD benchmark. Compared to LLMLingua-2, D2L performs roughly similarly to compressing the context down to 40% of its original length"
  where: Sec 5.1.1, p5.
- Needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH) generalizes beyond the training length and beyond the base model's window. D2L trained on 32-256 token contexts (1-8 chunks) holds near-perfect accuracy to 40 chunks (about 40K tokens). The base gemma-2-2b-it has an 8K window and collapses above it.
  number: 40K tokens; training max 256 tokens; more than 4x the native window
  setup: RULER-style 4-digit "magic number" needle; chunk size 1024 tokens; simplified training (cross-entropy, same query as at evaluation, 640K samples, about 3 h on one H200).
  quote: "performance remains close to perfect up to 40 chunks (40K tokens), which is quintuple the number of chunks the model has been exposed to during its training phase. Beyond this point, performance begins to degrade gracefully."
  where: Sec 4, p4.
- Generation-time memory is small and independent of document length. The base model needs more than 12 GB of extra memory at a 128K-token haystack. The internalized model uses under 50 MB.
  number: more than 12 GB vs < 50 MB
  setup: NIAH, gemma-2-2b-it.
  quote: "The base model uses more than 12 GB of additional memory to generate a response to a 128K-token haystack. In contrast, the model with internalized knowledge consistently uses significantly lower memory (< 50 MB)"
  where: Sec 4, p5.
- Long-document QA (2WikiMultihopQA) works zero-shot on documents up to 32K tokens, although the longest training sample is 2,344 tokens. D2L almost matches oracle CD and uses far less update memory and time than CD with generated queries.
  number: normalized performance 0.857 (D2L batched), 0.844 (iterative), 0.901 (oracle CD), 0.745 (CD 25 queries), 0.704 (CD 5 queries); update memory 11.522 / 3.791 / 7.820 / 59.925 / 79.371 GB; latency 0.209 / 0.551 / 40.171 / 465.454 / 72.537 s
  setup: LongBench 2WikiMultihopQA, gemma-2-2b-it; CD queries come from truncated documents.
  quote (Table 1 rows): "CD(oracle query)0.901 7.820 40.171±0.351 / D2L(batched)0.85711.5220.209±0.123 / D2L(iterative)0.8443.7910.551±0.101 / CD(25 generated queries)0.745 59.925 465.454±67.868 / CD(5 generated queries)0.704 79.371 72.537±7.821"
  where: Table 1, p7; text p6.
- D2L stands in for CD with many queries. On a 100-sample SQuAD subset, CD improves with more queries but stays below D2L and takes minutes per document.
  number: CD 20/50/100 queries = 0.506 / 0.601 / 0.650 (latency 129 / 312 / 631 s); D2L 0.866 (0.086 s); oracle CD 0.988
  setup: SQuAD, 100 samples.
  quote: "its performance rises from 0.506 (20 queries) to 0.650 (100 queries). Crucially, CD with 100 queries takes more than 10 minutes to internalize each sample. In contrast, D2L achieves 0.866"
  where: Sec 6 and Table 4, p8.
- Update memory on short QA: D2L and oracle CD use under 2 GB. CD with generated queries uses over 40 GB.
  number: <2 GB vs >40 GB
  quote: "Both use less than 2 GB of VRAM during the update process across the three benchmarks. In contrast, CD with generated queries uses more than 40 GB"
  where: Sec 5.1.1, p6.
- Generation memory on long-document QA: in-context needs about 1 GB extra, and all in-parameter methods need under 100 MB.
  number: ~1 GB vs <100 MB
  quote: "the ICL baseline requires around 1 GB of VRAM while all in-parameter knowledge methods require less than 100 MB."
  where: Sec 5.1.2, p6.
- Reading the document directly after internalizing it can help. On 2WikiMultihopQA and MultiFieldQA, performance slightly improves when the model reads the truncated context again after D2L ("Ours + truncated context"). LLMLingua-2 at some rates also beats uncompressed truncated input. The authors attribute this to lost-in-the-middle or attention noise. This is a hypothesis, not a tested result.
  number: none
  quote: "we hypothesize that this might be because of the lost-in-the-middle (Liu et al., 2024) or attention noise (Ye et al., 2025) phenomena."
  where: Sec 5.1.2, p6-7.
- Training with a KL loss on the teacher's logits beats next-token prediction. Both rows are early (50%) checkpoints.
  number: SQuAD 0.819 vs 0.763; swapped recall 0.385 vs 0.235
  quote: "the KL variant outperforms the NTP variant on SQuAD, achieving a normalized F1 score of 0.819 compared to 0.763"
  where: App C.2, Table 6, p14.
- A larger rank helps. Rank 16 vs rank 8 gives SQuAD 0.896 vs 0.814 and DROP 0.711 vs 0.655. ROPES is the same (0.895 vs 0.906).
  quote: "D2L(rank-8) 0.814 0.655 0.906 / D2L(rank-16)0.896 0.711 0.895"
  where: Table 7, p15.
- Training data ablation: removing the QA data barely matters, except on DROP.
  number: DROP 0.574 vs 0.655; SQuAD 0.838 vs 0.814
  quote: "D2L w/o QA data 0.838 0.574 0.923"
  where: Table 5, p14.
- Knowledge interference is a real failure. When the stored context is irrelevant to the query, D2L does much worse than the base model and than CD.
  number: assistant prompt 0.096 vs base 0.201; distracting prompt 0.126 vs base 0.175 (CD 0.211 / 0.203)
  setup: SQuAD with the context replaced by "You are a useful assistant." or a roughly 4K-token Gutenberg chapter.
  quote: "Table 8 shows that D2L significantly reduces the performance compared to the base model and CD. We hypothesize that D2L might acquire a strong prior, assuming that the subsequent queries will always be related to the internalized knowledge."
  where: App C.4, p15.
- Cross-modal transfer: a VLM (gemma-3-4b-it) used as the encoder for a text-only target (gemma-2-2b-it) gets 75.03% on Imagenette (10-way classification, chance 10%). Text QA drops: SQuAD 0.814 to 0.705, DROP 0.655 to 0.568, ROPES 0.906 to 0.772.
  quote: "the target model gets 75.03% accuracy purely through the internalized information."
  where: Sec 5.2, Table 2, p7.
- Query internalization (the "swapped" test). Internalizing the query instead of the document gives recall 0.740 and precision 0.720 (base with context: 0.886 / 0.876). When the swapped model was used on the original task, recall was 0.587 and precision 0.044, because outputs are verbose. No-context baseline: recall 0.185.
  where: Table 3, p8.
- The architecture can also emit a compressed KV cache (prefix-tuning, 20 prefix tokens) instead of LoRA. Setup: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507. Result: near-perfect NIAH to 8K tokens, then graceful degradation. Generating keys directly degrades from about 4K tokens. Routing the keys through key-norm and RoPE sustains accuracy longer.
  quote: "it achieves near-perfect accuracy up to 8K tokens, beyond which performance degrades gracefully."
  where: App D, p18.
- Generality: D2L was also trained on Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, with similar findings. Exception: on Mistral-7B long-context QA, all internalization methods perform near the no-context baseline.
  quote: "We observe that all internalization methods struggle to update long context information for Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2."
  where: App E, p19.
- Versus Generative Adapter (Mistral-7B, SQuAD): GA has a higher F1 (0.632 vs D2L 0.515) but much lower recall (0.643 vs 0.835), because its answers are shorter. D2L's recall is 0.835 against the base model's 0.919.
  where: Table 12, p19.
- Training cost and recipe. About 3.2M unique contexts from FineWeb-Edu plus PwC, SQuAD, ROPES and DROP (about 900M tokens). 10 generated queries per FineWeb context from gemma-3-12b-it, and the response is sampled from gemma-2-2b-it with the top-16 logits kept. Two-stage training: 80K steps with single-chunk inputs, then 20K steps with chunking. Batches of over 200K context tokens across 8 GPUs; smaller batches converge too early.
  where: App B.1-B.2, p13-14.

LIMITS (authors' concessions plus what the source does not show)
- Meta-training is a single expensive phase. The Conclusion gives about 5 days on 8 H200 GPUs for gemma-2-2b-it.
- The hypernetwork must be retrained for each target LLM.
- A performance gap to in-context learning remains. Quote: "there is a performance gap between ICL and in-parameter knowledge methods, including D2L."
- The paper tests only LoRA, only small models (2B, 4B, 7B), and mostly extractive QA scored by ROUGE-L. The NIAH is a single 4-digit needle. NIAH training used a simplified setup (same query for training and evaluation, cross-entropy loss, activations from layer 6 only).
- Knowledge interference and the assumption that queries are always related to the stored context are unresolved. The authors suggest a fix (add irrelevant queries to training data) but do not test it.
- Several explanations are hypotheses, not tests: the lost-in-the-middle gains, the "emulates many queries" account, and no explanation for Mistral's long-context failure.
- CD baselines are budget-limited (5-25 generated queries). The authors say more queries "would likely boost CD performance beyond that of D2L".
- Results are normalized to the base model with context. Absolute scores are in Table 11, which I did not copy.
- There is no comparison to KV-cache compression or summarization/compaction of agent history. Compared prompt-compression baseline: LLMLingua-2 only. The paper is not about agent compaction. Possible weak links to note 05: it is a parametric alternative to in-context compression, and internalized text is not inspectable or editable, but the paper does not discuss either.
- The paper is a preprint from Feb 2026, so newer work may have superseded it.

BUILDS ON
- Context distillation: Askell et al. 2021; Choi et al. 2023; Padmanabhan et al. 2023; Snell et al. 2023; Bhargava et al. 2024 (Prompt Baking); Caccia et al. 2025; Eyuboglu et al. 2025 (Cartridges); Kujanpää et al. 2025; Qi et al. 2025; Shin et al. 2025.
- Hypernetworks (Ha et al. 2016); LoRA (Hu et al. 2022); Perceiver (Jaegle et al. 2021).
- Text-to-LoRA (Charakorn et al. 2025, the same group); Generative Adapter (Chen et al. 2025); MEND (Li et al. 2024); Gisting (Mu et al. 2024); prefix-tuning (Li & Liang 2021).
- Prompt compression: LLMLingua-2 (Pan et al. 2024), ICAE-style work (Chevalier et al. 2023).
- Benchmarks: RULER (Hsieh et al. 2024), LongBench (Bai et al. 2023), SQuAD, DROP, ROPES, QASPER, 2WikiMultihopQA, Imagenette; FineWeb-Edu data.
- Lost in the middle (Liu et al. 2024); attention noise (Ye et al. 2025).

CODE
Equations worth keeping: the CD objective (Eq. 2, p3) and the D2L meta-objective (Eq. 3-4, p3). Quote: "min_ϕ E(c,Dc)∼D E(x,y)∼Dc J(x,y,c), J(x,y,c) = KL( pθ(y|x,c) ∥ pθ+Hϕ(c)(y|x) )". Chunk composition (Eq. 9, p4) concatenates the per-chunk A and B along the rank dimension, giving total rank r·K. Pseudocode is in Listing 3 near the end (not read in full).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p2): training overview, plus performance, latency and memory versus CD on 2WikiMultihopQA and SQuAD.
- Fig 2 (p4): NIAH ROUGE-L versus haystack length (2^10 to 2^17) and extra memory. It shows the collapse of the base model past 8K and the flat memory.
- Fig 3 (p6): SQuAD performance versus context length ratio, update latency and memory, against LLMLingua-2 rates of 10-90%.
- Fig 4 (p7): long-document QA performance versus generation memory.
- Fig 5 (p13): training data length distribution (mean 277 tokens, max 2,344; 101M triplets).
- Fig 8 (p17): qualitative query-internalization outputs.
- Fig 9 (p18): KV-cache NIAH variant.

PROBLEMS: None serious. There are no embedded instructions in the PDF text. Ligatures and spacing are garbled in places (for example "proposeDoc-to-LoRA", "ﬁght"). Table cells run together in the extraction (for example "0.85711.5220.209" = 0.857 / 11.522 / 0.209), so I split them using the header order. Table 9 (MultiFieldQA) is reported against truncated ICL, not the base model, with D2L at about 0.48 against oracle CD at 1.041 and CD (25 queries) at 0.528. That is a weaker D2L result than the 2WikiMultihopQA one and should not be overlooked when citing. I did not run figures.py. The text dump is at /tmp/doclora.txt.
